title: Conflicting transcripts — one says the extractor works, the next says it does not
why: Two voice notes from the same room contradict each other on the extractor. The finding must not state either as fact; the verifier should surface the conflict; if EXTRACT-FAN-REPLACE is proposed it must be flagged for the surveyor, not silently priced.

room.name: Bathroom
room.note: Mould to ceiling and upper walls.

transcripts: Bathroom, mould to the ceiling and top of the walls. Extractor fan's working fine, holds the paper, good draw.
Sorry, correction on the bathroom, extractor fan isn't working at all, it's not even spinning, no draw whatsoever.

must_not_happen.label: no flat statement that the fan works

must_not_happen.pattern: extractor( fan)? (was|is) (found|noted|observed) to be (not working|non-?operational|inoperative|not functioning)
must_not_happen.label: no flat statement that the fan is dead, without acknowledging the conflict
any fan line is an evidenced or flagged quantity

allowed_uncertainty: Either the later note is treated as a correction (and the prose says so) or the conflict is recorded and the fan line left for the surveyor. Both are acceptable. What is not acceptable is picking one silently.
reviewer_notes: Real surveyors do correct themselves on the next recording. The pipeline has no way to know which is right; it must show the surveyor both.
